title: Swim through the caves at Sawa-i-Lau
description: The second chamber is only reached by ducking through a short submerged passage with a local guide - the crew for The Blue Lagoon lit it with nothing but the natural skylight above.

title: Share a kava bowl in a Fijian village ceremony
description: Clap once before you drink, empty the coconut shell in one go, then clap three times after - Navala's thatched bure village in the highlands still runs the sevusevu properly rather than as a show for cruise groups.

title: Watch the Sawau tribe walk on white-hot stones
description: A hereditary gift said to come from a spirit god centuries ago, performed barefoot across stones heated for hours in a pit - only Sawau men from this one island are said to hold it.

title: Dive the soft corals of Rainbow Reef
description: The Somosomo Strait between Taveuni and Vanua Levu funnels current through the reef, and the soft corals only open into full colour on the running tide - ask the dive shop which window they're timing for.

title: Walk the shifting dunes at Sigatoka
description: Fiji's only national park protecting sand dunes, and also one of its largest archaeological sites - pottery and human remains over 2,600 years old keep surfacing as the wind reshapes them.

title: Eat your way through Suva's municipal market
description: Fiji's real capital rather than the resort coast - a two-storey market thick with kava roots, fire-roasted cassava and Indo-Fijian curry stalls, busiest and cheapest early on a Saturday.

title: Walk the wooden storefronts of old Levuka
description: Fiji's first colonial capital and now a UNESCO World Heritage town, barely changed since the 1880s - reachable only by a slow ferry or a rough road over Ovalau's interior.

title: Stand on the ash fields below Tavurvur volcano
description: The 1994 eruption buried the old town of Rabaul in ash and shifted the provincial capital to Kokopo - Tavurvur still smokes constantly, and a local guide is not optional given how fast conditions change.

title: Walk into the Japanese barge tunnels at Kokopo
description: Rabaul held over 100,000 Japanese troops by 1943, and the hand-dug tunnels built to hide barges and field hospitals from Allied bombing still run deep into the hillsides around Kokopo.

title: Watch a thousand tribes perform at the Goroka Show
description: PNG's biggest sing-sing, timed around Independence Day - clans that would never otherwise share a stage turn up in bird-of-paradise plumes and clay paint to out-perform each other for a weekend.

title: See the highlands sing-sing at the Mount Hagen Show
description: Started in the 1960s to defuse tribal fighting by turning rivalry into performance - hundreds of groups still travel for days on foot to compete in war paint that took hours to apply.

title: Watch the yam harvest festival on the Trobriand Islands
description: Anthropologist Malinowski's 'Islands of Love' - a matrilineal society whose yam harvest is marked by competitive Milamala dancing, and the real challenge is simply finding a boat or charter flight out here.

title: Watch the land divers of Pentecost Island
description: The original bungee jump - men dive head-first off 20m wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles, timed to the yam harvest. The vine length is judged by eye alone, and it has gone wrong before.

title: Drink kava at a Port Vila nakamal at dusk
description: Ni-Vanuatu kava is stronger and drunk in near silence, unlike the social bowls elsewhere in the Pacific - order a shell, spit once, drink it in one go, and expect your lips to go numb.

title: Walk a bush-medicine trail through Ekasup village
description: A short drive from the resorts but run entirely by the custom village it sits in - a demonstration of pig-killing ceremony, bush medicine and hunting traps rather than a show staged for cruise days.

title: Walk the 25km lagoon beach at Ouvea
description: Often rated among the best beaches on earth and among the least visited - a 1988 hostage crisis kept tourism away for years, and the Kanak community here still controls access to parts of the island.

title: Walk among giant kauri and the drowned forest at Riviere Bleue
description: A dam flooded part of the forest decades ago, leaving dead trunks standing in the lake water - also one of the last strongholds of the kagu, a flightless bird found nowhere else on earth.

title: Ride to the Vaipo waterfall in the Hakaui Valley
description: One of the tallest waterfalls in French Polynesia, reached by boat then a hike up a valley so steep and narrow the sun barely gets in - the Marquesas get a fraction of the visitors Tahiti does.

title: Find Gauguin's grave above Atuona
description: Paul Gauguin and Jacques Brel are buried a few metres apart in a small hillside cemetery above the harbour, both having chosen to end their lives on one of the most remote inhabited island groups on earth.

title: Feed the sacred blue-eyed eels at Faie
description: Freshwater eels over a metre long with genuinely blue eyes, considered sacred by the village and fed by hand from the bridge - Huahine also holds some of the best-preserved marae temples in the Society Islands.

title: Tour a vanilla plantation on Taha'a
description: Taha'a grows most of French Polynesia's vanilla, hand-pollinated flower by flower since its natural pollinator doesn't exist here - it shares a lagoon with Raiatea and gets none of Bora Bora's crowds.

title: Climb Mount Vaea to Robert Louis Stevenson's grave
description: Stevenson built his last home here and is buried on the summit above it, exactly where he asked to be - his Samoan name, Tusitala, means teller of tales.

title: Swim the cave pool at Piula
description: A freshwater pool inside a lava cave next to a theological college, connected to the ocean through an underwater passage that only confident swimmers should attempt.

title: Walk the ring road of car-free Manono Island
description: No cars and barely any noise - a 90-minute circuit on foot past four villages, with Apolima and Savai'i visible across the strait the whole way round.

title: Stand under the Ha'amonga 'a Maui trilithon
description: Coral limestone slabs weighing up to 40 tonnes each, raised around 1200AD for a king with no written record of how it was done - sometimes called the Stonehenge of the Pacific, though nobody agrees on its purpose.

title: Walk the rainforest and sea cliffs of 'Eua
description: A short ferry from Tongatapu but geologically its opposite number, uplifted rather than volcanic - caves, a colony of flying foxes you can watch leave at dusk, and cliffs used to spot migrating humpbacks.

title: Crawl into Anatakitaki cave on Atiu
description: Home to the kopeka, a swiftlet found nowhere else, which echolocates in total darkness like a bat - the tour ends with a swim in an underground pool most visitors don't expect.

title: Hear the hymn harmonies at a Rarotonga Sunday service
description: Visitors are genuinely welcome at the CICC churches, and the unaccompanied four-part harmony is one of the most striking things you'll hear in the Pacific - dress modestly and stay for the whole service.

title: Walk Bloody Ridge above Honiara
description: Also called Edson's Ridge - a few hundred US Marines held this position against repeated night assaults in 1942, a turning point in the Guadalcanal campaign. Rusting artillery still sits in the grass.

title: Track turtles and hornbills on Tetepare Island
description: The largest uninhabited island in the South Pacific, protected by the descendants of the people who once left it, who now run it as a community conservation project rather than sell the logging rights.

title: Swim the royal bathing chasm at Matapa
description: A narrow, sheer-walled inlet once reserved for Niuean royalty to bathe in - calm at low tide, dangerous in a swell, and a five-minute walk from Talava.

title: Walk through the Talava Arches
description: A collapsed sea cave leaving a set of limestone arches on Niue's wildest coast, reached by a track through the Huvalu forest that keeps almost everyone away.

title: Find the Japanese bunkers on Betio beach
description: The Battle of Tarawa in 1943 killed more than 6,000 people in 76 hours - concrete bunkers and rusting guns still sit in the sand where the fighting stopped, mostly unmarked and unfenced.

title: Snorkel the WWII wrecks in Funafuti lagoon
description: US forces built the airstrip that is now Funafuti's runway in 1943 - wrecked aircraft and landing craft from that build-up still lie in the shallow lagoon a short swim from shore.

title: Walk the freshwater lagoon at Buada
description: Nauru's only body of fresh water, sitting in a subsided pit left by phosphate mining, ringed with banana and pandanus that a century of strip-mining left almost nowhere else on the island.

title: Walk into the phosphate pinnacles of Topside
description: A century of phosphate mining stripped the island's interior to a moonscape of coral limestone pinnacles - Nauru was briefly the highest per-capita income country on earth because of it, and one of the poorest soon after.

title: Walk the WWII battlefield on Peleliu
description: One of the bloodiest and most disputed battles of the Pacific war, fought over an island of questionable strategic value - rusted tanks, planes and artillery still lie in the jungle at Bloody Nose Ridge exactly where they stopped.

title: Coat yourself in mud at the Milky Way
description: A lagoon of pale limestone mud said to be a natural skin treatment - scoop it from the seabed, coat yourself, dry off in the sun, then rinse in water so turquoise it looks tinted.

title: Dive with manta rays in the German Channel
description: A channel blasted through the reef by German phosphate miners a century ago, now a cleaning station where reef mantas circle divers for as long as the current allows.

title: See the stone money banks of Yap
description: Giant carved limestone discs, some over 3m across, still hold real value and change ownership without moving - the village simply agrees who owns which one, and it stays exactly where it was quarried.

title: Walk the basalt ruins of Lelu
description: A walled royal and religious complex built with the same basalt-log technique as Nan Madol, on an islet now joined to Kosrae's main town by causeway and largely reclaimed by jungle.

title: Dive the wrecks of Kwajalein Atoll
description: One of the largest lagoons on earth by enclosed area, and the site of a brutal 1944 battle before it became a US missile-testing base - Japanese wrecks sit alongside a still-active military range.

title: Walk the invasion beach at War in the Pacific park
place: War in the Pacific National Historical Park
description: US forces landed here in 1944 to retake Guam after two and a half years of Japanese occupation - the Asan Bay Overlook and the gun emplacements above it are the clearest place in Micronesia to grasp the scale of the war.

title: Stand at the cliff of Two Lovers Point
description: A Chamorro legend of two lovers who leapt rather than be separated - now a glass-floored overlook above Tumon Bay, busiest at sunset.

title: Snorkel the reef flat at Tumon Bay
description: A shallow, current-free reef right off Guam's main hotel strip - easy enough for a first snorkel, though the coral closest to shore shows decades of sunscreen and foot traffic.

title: Reach the wild north coast at Ritidian Point
description: A wildlife refuge at Guam's northern tip protecting the island's last strip of undeveloped reef and beach, with limestone forest and nesting sea turtles where the rest of the island has long since been built over.

title: Eat kelaguen at the Chamorro Village night market
description: A Wednesday-night street market in the capital with barbecue, red rice and kelaguen - grilled meat cured in lemon, chilli and coconut - alongside live Chamorro dance.

title: Hike the ridge above Vatia in the National Park of American Samoa
description: The only US national park south of the equator, and one of the least visited in the entire system - rainforest running straight down to the reef, with flying foxes overhead in daylight instead of at dusk.

title: Snorkel the reef off Ofu Beach
description: Regularly named among the best beaches in the US national park system and among the emptiest - getting to the Manu'a group at all takes a small plane or a boat, which is exactly why it stays this way.

title: Watch seabirds nest on Pola Island
description: A sheer volcanic islet just off Vatia village, too steep for predators to reach, so red-footed boobies and other seabirds nest on it in full view from the shore.

title: Stand at Banzai Cliff and Suicide Cliff
description: In 1944, told by their own propaganda that surrender meant torture, hundreds of Japanese civilians and soldiers jumped from these cliffs rather than face the advancing US forces. Memorials from several nations now stand at the top.

title: Dive the sunbeams inside The Grotto
description: A collapsed limestone cavern reached by a steep staircase and a swim through a narrow entrance, opening into shafts of light that regularly rank it among Asia-Pacific's best dive sites - and among its more dangerous on a rough day.

title: Stand in the pits where the atomic bombs were loaded
description: Enola Gay and Bockscar were loaded from these two concrete pits at what was briefly the busiest airfield in the world - Tinian now has a few thousand residents and North Field is largely reclaimed by jungle.

title: Take the boat to Managaha Island
description: A small uninhabited islet inside Saipan's lagoon, ringed by a reef shallow enough to wade, and considered sacred ground by Chamorro and Carolinian islanders alike.

title: Look into the crater lake at Lalolalo
description: A volcanic crater lake ringed by 80m cliffs, with the remains of a WWII American anti-aircraft battery still standing at the rim from when Wallis was a Pacific staging base nobody now remembers.

title: Visit the basilica of Saint-Pierre-Chanel on Futuna
description: Built where the missionary Pierre Chanel was killed in 1841, later canonised as the South Pacific's only Catholic martyr-saint - a pilgrimage site most of the world has never heard of.

title: Sail 24 hours to Tokelau on the supply ship
description: No airstrip exists or is planned - the only way in is an overnight sailing from Apia on the government vessel, landing by small boat since none of the three atolls has a harbour large ships can enter.

title: Swim the lagoon at Nukunonu
description: The largest of Tokelau's three atolls by land area, its motu linked by causeways, in one of the least visited territories on the planet - a few dozen tourists a year, by most estimates.

title: Land at Bounty Bay and walk Adamstown
description: Home to around 40 people, nearly all descended from the Bounty mutineers and their Tahitian companions - the ship's anchor and a cannon, salvaged from Bounty Bay, sit outside the courthouse.

title: Climb to Christian's Cave above Adamstown
description: Fletcher Christian is said to have sat here watching the horizon for ships that might find him - reaching Pitcairn at all means a supply ship from Mangareva that runs only a few times a year.

title: Climb to the Cristo Rei statue above Dili
description: A 27m statue on a headland east of Dili, built during Indonesian occupation and now flanked by a stairway with stations of the cross - a quiet beach sits on the far side away from the city.

title: Climb Mount Ramelau for sunrise
description: Timor-Leste's highest point, climbed overnight so pilgrims and trekkers reach the Virgin Mary statue at the summit before dawn - on a clear morning you can see both coasts of the island at once.
